limits: For white wine, Pinot Gris: at most 10%
For red and rosé wine, the minor grapes together: at most 15%
rules.yield_base: 60 hl/ha for rosé, 57 for white, 50 for red

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Gris sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

blurb.text: A Côte de Nuits appellation, the only village appellation allowed to make rosé. Red wine, about two-thirds of production, and rosé use Pinot Noir, and white uses Chardonnay. It has no Grand Cru or Premier Cru vineyards.
